spine.last_session: Relicensed the tree to Apache 2.0 matching logbook: LICENSE verified byte-identical by sha256, NOTICE rewritten keeping the kickstart MIT carve-out, package.json set to Apache-2.0, README updated, and ai.txt, robots.txt and tdmrep.json deleted. Nothing committed.

open_risks.text: Do not commit the working tree as one change — README.md holds two unrelated lines of work at once, so a single commit makes the relicense impossible to review against the licence files it changes

Do not merge the relicense branch until the docs branch it stacks on has been deleted — GitHub retargets a stacked child only on base deletion, so it would otherwise merge into a dead branch and never reach main

The Apache grant on any published version is permanent — later commits can carry a different licence, but anyone who fetched the Apache version keeps those rights, so a revert changes the terms only going forward
Do not stage .superpowers/ — it is untracked in the working tree and a blanket git add would sweep it into whichever commit runs first

out_of_scope: The docs refactor and the config edits sharing this working tree — they predate this thread and belong to their own commits, not to the relicense.
Legal advice on the licence change — this thread implements the owner's choice and states its consequences; it is not a legal opinion.
